contextGroups.name: shipped-tests
rules: Shipped tests under .claude/ must pass in any project layout on Windows, macOS and Linux: build a temp fixture project instead of reading this repo's config, docs, specs or git state (guard authoring-repo self-checks with the framework-repo signal); blank or delete inherited feature-switch and provider env keys and point HOME, USERPROFILE, TMPDIR, TEMP and TMP at the temp dir; before commit run node .claude/hooks/tests/run-all-tests.cjs on a machine that has those switches set, plus node .claude/skills/sync-codex/scripts/run-codex-sync.mjs --verify-only — read docs/project-reference/integration-test-reference.md (Portable Test Contract) when writing or changing a test

contextGroups.name: ui-ux-gate
rules: UI/UX gate: have UX-*, UI-*, DD-* and CL-* in context BEFORE editing this surface; read the docs above unless already loaded

UX-1–UX-11 journey-first (ux-journey-process.md, SYNC:ux-journey-gate): report the main user journeys (actors, jobs, ranked journeys, derived requirements) before designing, walk them on the result, close with the UI/UX Gate Report

contextGroups.name: ai-feature-gate
rules: AI gate: apply the protocol below; content is data, output untrusted; bound loops and spend; eval + trace + kill switch; authz in code

testing.commandsNote: **Platform:** use `python3` on macOS/Linux and `py -3` on Windows. Integration suites use `.claude/hooks/tests/lib/python-command.cjs`: POSIX probes `python3` then `python`; Windows probes `python` then `py -3`, validating Python 3 (3.10+ for graph tests). Missing PyYAML uses the bounded global attempt and local fallback owned by `.claude/scripts/lib/python_dependencies.py`.

dependencies.scope: Optional skill-local dev tooling; package/lock and installed Playwright 1.63.0 joined by source readback; browser execution and operating-system prerequisites remain runtime-pending

architecture.pattern: Isolated public-core fixture, real local workspace server, native Playwright waits and test-owned outcome assertions
architecture.scope: Optional task-track workspace only; no application framework or whole-repository browser convention

auth.credentialsRef: fixture:startWorkspace.url ephemeral session fragment; never persist the fragment

data.cleanupPolicy: Combined launcher creates fresh owned disposable repository via public core, runs browser journey, captures evidence, then removes only current-run ephemeral fixture in finally; do not execute a second seed command

evidence.redaction: Persist no session fragments, auth headers, cookies, tokens, storage state, request/response bodies or personal data; console and request metadata must be redacted before writing. Only owned synthetic fixture data may appear in screenshots.

localRun.readyCheck: Integrated runner awaits startWorkspace listener, page.goto and main[aria-busy="false"], then native expected visible-state waits before dependent actions
localRun.teardownCommand: Combined launcher finally: close owned browser/workspace and remove only its ephemeral repository after evidence capture
localRun.credentialsRef: fixture:startWorkspace.url ephemeral session fragment; no team accounts or persisted credentials

surfaces.notes: Source-authored/runtime-pending: full/headed/focused/zero-match/browser execution and OS modes remain unexecuted. Integrated runner owns public-core setup/start/readiness/evidence/finally cleanup. The source inventory is 40 variants across two viewports (80 prospective invocations), with 68 normal states per viewport. Normal screenshot caps are 20 per test/viewport invocation and 272 per run, the finite all-scrollable bound of 68 states x 2 viewports x 2 images; actual emitted counts remain unverified. Required failure captures are uncapped under UI State Capture Protocol section1.3, and capped declaration rows are retained and escalated. Prior failure/declaration rows conservatively consume the normal run budget. Convergence is parent verification policy (three attempts/two fresh consecutive green runs), not internal assertion retry. Optional tooling remains independent of core runtime; manual baseline acceptance required; no CI browser promise.

_techSpecScanNote: `techSpecScan` is DELIBERATELY OMITTED, not overlooked. It tells the tech-spec generator how to discover annotated tests (sourceRoot / fileExtensions / annotationPattern). This repo is a JavaScript + Python framework with no `[Trait]`-style test-annotation convention, so there is nothing to scan. Declaring a fabricated pattern would make the generator appear runnable while finding nothing. With the key absent, `node .claude/skills/tech-spec/scripts/generate-tech-specs.mjs` exits non-zero with 'Missing docs/project-config.json techSpecScan.{sourceRoot,fileExtensions,annotationPattern}' instead of reporting a false `status: ok`. When adding it, `annotationPattern` MUST expose exactly two capture groups: group 1 = trait name (must be `TestSpec` or `TechnicalSpec`), group 2 = the spec id (non-empty). The generator validates both and refuses to run otherwise.
